blocks.text: My role @ LEGO House

At LEGO House, I held a hybrid role as Experience Design lead and Senior Product Manager for the pre- and post-visit experience. I was responsible for shaping the end-to-end guest journey—before, during, and after the visit by combining physical, digital, and service touch points into one cohesive experience. I owned the digital guest journey at LEGO House, connecting pre- and post-visit experiences into one unified end user experience.
Key contributions included:

items: Introducing and implementing service design as a core practice, aligning internal teams around guest journeys, service blueprints, and operational touch points.
Leading the UX and experience strategy across interactive installations, digital platforms, and support services

Driving product discovery and delivery for pre- and post-visit experiences such as planning tools, personalised content, and memory creation. This role was loosely designed structured to embedding service design thinking into how LEGO House serves its guests holistically.

My role was to manage the digital and service touch points before and after a guest visits LEGO House from ticketing and planning to post-visit memories and re-engagement.

caseStudies.title: LEGO House Ticketing Migration
caseStudies.subtitle: Rebuilding the foundation to enable future growth and flexibility

blocks.text: Overview

When LEGO House first opened, the ticketing system was built to support a brand-new attraction with relatively predictable needs. Over seven years, the way guests planned, booked, and experienced their visits changed significantly, and the system gradually began to show its limits. By 2024, it was clear that the platform had outgrown what it was originally designed for, making everyday operations harder and limiting how the experience could evolve. Migrating the ticketing system at LEGO House became a necessary step to meet today’s demand and support the experiences guests now expect.
Challenges
Out dated tech backbone. Bespoke & rigid for changes.
Unreliable, Often had downtime when there were high load.
No support from the vendor (previous) leaving us helpless.
Guest ops team had to mobilise resources from time to time.
Unable to scale products to 9+ different ticket types.
Solution

In order to support growth ambition, we replaced current custom-built solution with a market-ready, off-the-shelf platform from Visit Group . This allowed us to adopt a proven ticketing foundation while focusing our efforts on configuration, integration, and experience quality rather than maintaining bespoke infrastructure.
Discovery
6 teams were impacted by the platform change that served 7 years ! Some felt relieved and for some it was a new opportunity
Guest Touch points impacted in the migration

The ticketing system sat at the core of LEGO House , influencing every part of its day-to-day operation. From guest entry and capacity planning to retail, experiences, and post-visit touchpoints. To understand the full impact of changing this backbone system, I created a holistic journey map by working closely with department heads across operations, guest services, retail, and other teams. These conversations helped surface hidden dependencies, pain points, and risks, allowing us to see the system not just as technology, but as a connected experience across people, processes, and platforms.
Roadmap & Rollout Strategy
Stage 1 : Launch AFOL Day tickets Test Hero/Core Flow
Purchase ticket - Redeem wrist bands - Enter LH Gates - Experience zones - Exit
Stage 2 : Fix all bells & whistles Test Peripherals
Partner Integrations - API’s - Kiosks - Gates - Help desk - exit - Memories
Stage 3 : Go all in Full launch
Outcome
Improved system stability
Faster turn around for changes
Allowed us to grow to 360K Guests
Better Revenue protection during peak seasons
Reduced operational and support overhead
Frictionless flow across Kiosk and gates & Exp: zones
2.5x more footprints on our memories
Before
After
Learnings

items: Clear ownership is required to reduce, ambiguity.
Involving legal, and accounts early helps fast track the process.
Trust-building matters – Addressing security concerns helped increase conversions.

Create prioritised list based on user feedbacks and stakeholder input
Identify new opportunities working with stakeholders & exec: leadership

blocks.text: Overview

Skyfish is a digital asset management (DAM) platform that helps teams store, organise, and distribute visual content at scale. It is used by organisations that rely heavily on images and videos. It is mostly used by marketing teams where speed, consistency, and governance are essential.

Skyfish also handles the contractual and usage rights tied to images, helping businesses stay compliant and avoid legal risk. By tracking licenses, usage terms, and expiry conditions alongside each asset, the platform ensures content is used correctly across channels. This combination of asset management and rights control allows teams to work confidently, knowing their visual content is both accessible and legally safe, while being highly collaborative.
Skyfish is Scandinavia's most trusted brands among major corporations and public sectors like all Kommunes in Denmark, Norway & other Scandinavian countries. DSB, Novo nordisk, SKAT, Nordea etc.
Problem

Over time, Skyfish’s technology stack had begun to show its age. Years of incremental additions had resulted in a tightly coupled, spaghetti-like codebase, making even small changes risky and time consuming. This slowed down development, limited scalability, and made it increasingly difficult to evolve the product in response to user and business needs, despite the experience itself still being valued by customers.
Solution

We took a decision to modernise the tech architecture without disrupting experience. The solution was a complete re-architecture of the platform, decoupling core systems and keep the overall experience similar. As we migrated, we introduced small, improvements where it made sense. This approach allowed us a smooth transition for existing customers.
Role
Head of Product Design
Tools
Figma, Miro
Team
2 UX designers, 4 developers
Challeneges

When I joined Skyfish, the product was not in a good state. Years of accumulated technical and design debt, spaghetti code, where even small changes took an enormous amount of time and coordination. Product decisions were constrained by technology, requiring repeated alignment with engineering just to understand what was feasible.

This had a direct impact on the business. Customers were loosing trust, with a churn rate of around 10%, and several key product areas were still stuck in an MVP state. Users were vocal about their dissatisfaction with the core experience, while the team struggled to move fast enough to respond.

One of the biggest challenges was breaking this cycle, creating alignment between product, design, and engineering, and influencing a shift in technical direction that would allow faster decision-making and meaningful progress again.
Step1: Creating a shared awarness

The first step was to bring the organisation together around a shared understanding of the problem. While symptoms showed up in the user experience, delivery speed, and churn, the root cause was largely hidden in the underlying tech stack.

To make this visible, I initiated a cross-functional workshop where product, design, engineering, and business stakeholders jointly mapped the as-is customer journey. By walking through real scenarios and identifying friction points end to end, it became clear how technical constraints were shaping and often limiting the experience.

This exercise helped shift the conversation from isolated issues to systemic problems. It created alignment, reduced finger-pointing, and built a common language for why change was necessary setting the foundation for decisions around architecture, priorities, and pace moving forward at Skyfish.
Journey mapping & identifying frictions to be address in an AS-IS map
Step2: Resolve tech stack and design govenrance

We moved the front end to React.js and introduced a new design system built on top of MUI ( mui.com ), customised to Skyfish’s visual language and product needs. This gave us a well-supported component library.

Alongside the tech shift, we established clearer design governance. Shared components, patterns, and interaction rules were documented and maintained in a central design library, reducing duplication and guesswork.
Surveys

The core promise of Skyfish is simple: making image storage and usage easy, safe, and dependable for teams. My role was to reconnect everyday design decisions back to that promise, and to ensure every interaction added real impact for user.

By reframing the product around end-to-end workflows and user intent not isolated screens, we were able to enhance key interactions. This shift helped move conversations from “why can’t we build this?” to “does this make storing and using images easier for our users?” , creating stronger alignment and better decisions across the team.
For
Example ...
Before - 2020
After - 2023
Impact
https://www.youtube.com/embed/22vXVVbn4sM

items: 12% higher feature adoption resulting in DKK 4 million revenue growth.
Clearer value proposition for business; reduced sales cycle from 9 months to 6.

blocks.text: Overview

LEGO House was going through an evaluation period of a 4 year long strategic initiatives. This was the time when all the tech has been rebuilt in the house, and was the perfect storm period to look at how to improve the guest experience with the new tech backbone. This when we decided to conduct a time bound journey mapping exercise.

We wanted to understanding the guest from the outside in. Also to explore how the experience is actually lived, felt and navigated by different types of guests, pre, during and post. Based on that understanding, we define the as-is journey and provide a clear view of the underlying pain points that shape it. Along the way, we also identify the moments that create emotional lift and deep connection. We call these magic makers. They are what make the experience unforgettable and should be protected and amplified as the journey evolves.
State of affair State of affair today
Methodology
IMMERSIVE FIELDWORK
Over a period of two months we have conducted a multitude of observations, semi-structured and structured interviews talking to and observing guests from Bermuda to Ballerup.
PATTEN CLUSTERING

Triangulated data from interviews, behaviour and observations analysed and clustered with the LEGO House team. Identified key dynamics across the journey, including friction points and emotional highs.
SYNTHESIS & MAPPING
Insights condensed into an as-is guest journey and thematic clusters. Designed to inform the next phase: to- be journey mapping and opportunity space exploration.
Brief interviews, with 12 nationalities
Semi structured interviews, with 7 nationalities
100+ HOURS
Desktop research: internal docs., brand assets, etc.
200+ HOURS
Data triangulation: from interviews & observations
Outcome: AS-IS Guest journey map
Thematic categories

We clustered all the guest signals into themes. Pre and post- experiences are clustered in temporal themes since the journey is linear at this point. Themes during the visit are cross-cutting reflecting the free flow of the house. Each theme is presented as pain points, tensions, or unmet needs (the pink slides) and as opportunity spaces and early solutions (the yellow slides). An opportunity emerges when a theme shows potential for improvement, and a solution is a specific response to that opportunity. One solution can often address multiple “themes”. The themes make up the foundation for the Dream Bigger scenarios. After prioritisation move into full ideation and look on possible solutions for the chosen scenarios. Thematic categories helped prioritise strategic priorities for further investments of a 4 year strategy cycle.
10 Thematic areas to invest in ...
My role ...

items: Developed research briefs for partners to follow.
Create research protocols in collaboration with partners to conduct ethnographic studies, interviews, and guest observations ensuring rigour and alignment with LEGO’s Brand standards.
Creating Strategic Alignment: Aligned stakeholders across operations, product, tech, and brand to co-own service challenges and co-create solutions.
Ensure timely completions and project success.
Scaling and Coaching: Mentored designers in adopting service thinking and rituals to make service design repeatable and scalable.

caseStudies.title: LEGO House Access
caseStudies.subtitle: From Entry to Exit: Rethinking Access at LEGO House

blocks.text: Overview

At LEGO House, the wristband is far more than an entry pass, it is the backbone of the entire experience. From the moment a guest enters, the wristband carries essential user information and acts as a single point of access across the house.

Using RFID scanning, the wristband seamlessly recognises and validates guests at different touchpoints, allowing them to move freely and enjoy experiences without friction. Every scan quietly connects the physical and digital worlds, enabling play, participation, and personalisation throughout the visit.

The wristband also holds the key to memories. When guests return home, it unlocks the creations and moments they made inside LEGO House extending the experience beyond the visit itself. Without the wristband, there is no LEGO House experience; it carries both the weight of access and the emotional value of memories.
The real Challenge
Users had to solve a puzzle to access their memories, due to which not many attempted to access !!!

Guests needed to keep either of the two visitor materials to access memories, This was causing less users to access their memories. Also guests were not aware that they had to preserve these guest materials.
Solution
Transforming a Clunky Process into a Seamless Memory Journey : A Simple 2 step process
What did it take to achieve the solution

It required aligning the right people, resources, and timing to make meaningful progress. To move away from friction and give guests better experience, I had to rally the right people , shape the vision, and build the momentum for change. Here are some milestones achieved by me in order to get to final result.

Overview

Around 2015–2016, AT&T was experiencing explosive growth in connected vehicles, with major automobile manufacturers relying on AT&T to power in-car connectivity. At any given time, close to 30 million SIMs were active across automotive clients alone. While the network scaled successfully, the operational side had not anticipated the volume and complexity of service requests that would follow, specially around connectivity issues, diagnostics, and lifecycle management.

As device volumes increased, so did customer support escalations. Troubleshooting connectivity problems was slow, fragmented, and heavily dependent on manual processes and internal tools not designed for this scale. The lack of real-time visibility into device status quickly became a critical business risk, impacting both AT&T teams and their automotive partners.

Recognising this gap, AT&T decided to invest in a dedicated digital platform that would allow enterprises to monitor, manage, and diagnose connectivity at scale. Our team was commissioned to design and deliver this IoT connection management platform, transforming how connectivity was monitored, issues were identified, and service teams responded, moving from reactive support to proactive, data-driven operations.
Role
Design Leader & Strategist
Team
2 UX / UI designers, 4 developers
Timeline
9 Months
Challenges
AT&T saw rapid growth in its IoT division, mainly due to demand in connected vehicles and millions of active SIMs that connects them.
While connectivity scaled, core capabilities, device provisioning, SIM/eSIM management, and connectivity tracking, remained fragmented.

The lack of visibility resulted in delayed diagnosing issues which takes up to a week. Additionally overwhelming engineering teams and impacting customer trust. This growing gap between scale and operational readiness made a unified IoT management platform essential.
Insights + Alignment

To start designing a solution that worked at scale (Billions of device monitor-ability) we studied the full lifecycle of a SIM from commissioning to decommissioning across systems, teams, and real-world workflows at AT&T. We combined PRDs, stakeholder interviews, workshops, whiteboard sessions, and system walkthroughs to map how work actually happened, not how it was documented.

By abstracting each stage of the lifecycle, we surfaced critical service moments and friction points engineers faced when switching between operational, diagnostic, and service roles. Inputs from MNO admins, OEM admins, engineers, and operations teams revealed recurring needs around visibility, safety, traceability, and confidence when working with live systems.

These insights became the foundation for identifying where failures occurred, what needed protection, and where proactive monitoring and automation could replace manual effort—directly shaping our “how might we” problem framing and solution direction.
Insight Synthesis

We combined PRDs, stakeholder interviews, workshops, whiteboard sessions, and system walkthroughs to map how work actually happened, not how it was documented.
Concept Explorations

We explored multiple concepts to see what felt most natural for users managing complex systems. By testing layouts, navigation, and information density with real users, we focused on reducing friction and cognitive load. The final design was chosen for its clarity and familiarity, making tasks feel simpler, and faster.

Background

The Manorama Yearbook is a treasure trove of information widely referred by one who are preparing for UPSC exams* and other keen readers.We created a comprehensive platform which provides one stop solution to all aspirants while retaining the 53-year-old legacy of Manorama Yearbook of being a trusted content provider.

*UPSC Exams are the screening process for public services in India where successful candidates holds most powerful positions nationally like District collectors, Head of police, Foriegn Ambassadors etc. More than 500,000 aspirant each year compete for 980 vacancies in UPSC Civil Services.

The original remit of the Yearbook was to bridge the gap between knowledge divide that existed in the society. Over the years the Yearbook has proved to be a perfect guide for students by providing unique perspectives on general knowledge & current affairs.
My Role & Team

I am the design strategist in the project, My responsibilities were: to be in touch key stakeholders of the company & define foundation for their first digital experience. Set direction for the team, monitor the progress time to time, set guidelines for the team, involve hands on & help team in design detailing, mentor team for successful execution. My team involved 2 Designers, 1UI Developer & 1 Design lead:
Challenges

In the age of free news & content the challenge was to figure out a unique experience for General knowledge & Current affairs. The space was crowded with online media houses, news aggregators & traditional news media houses. It was distraction for serious aspirants to get the right information.
Another major challenge is aspirants today has multiple silos that he/she has to access to get a comprehensive picture of current affairs.
Yearly editions of Manorama Yearbook
Foundation
Stakeholder Workshop
Basis: Identify key users and assess the current state, brainstorm on possible foundational building blocks for the product. Align the team with a common goal.
Motive: Enable design team to familiarise with and strategise solution, recommend value additions to client's product in order to create a digital "yearbook" experience.
Significance: Help & guide client understand the digital behaviour patterns & align the business, to cater new set of digital audience.
Activities: Business canvas, Empathy mapping, Day in life of the user, user journey map, competition study.
Persona

The following persona's were uncovered during workshop. Various future state scenarios of product usage were considered to develop a picture. We mapped "day in life" of user to evaluate influence of different form factors during the day to arrive at a usage pattern.
Day in life of persona's identified to inform design
Mental model

Since the preparation for UPSC is a long drawn process which requires great amount of perseverance, we wanted to understand various emotional journey the user is subjected to. This further can inform our design, also helps how we plan our feature functionalities.
User mental model to inform design.
User journey map
Future state of user jouney was traced from discovery to purchase phase. This activity helped in identifying key flows and touch points which users will come across.
Journey map of both buyer & non-buyer
Research
Contextual inquiry

To understand the lifestyle of UPSC aspirants more closely, Think Design team conducted primary research and spent a day with an UPSC aspirants preparing to appear in forthcoming examinations. By using Questionnaire and Photo Elicitation method useful insights were drawn.
Contextual inquiry
Strategy
Opportunity areas
Through the discovery we have identified opportunity areas that can create an impact in users exam preparation. Opportunity areas were uncovered to help focus on effective concept development.

360 degree experience: Cover all aspects of UPSC preparation & bring it all together for end user consumption. Currently users have silos of activities, consolidation itself is a big value add in this domain.
Rethink content anatomy: Catering to multiple persona types, means address needs of multiple users. Rethinking the content anatomy helps address diverse users.

Self evaluation & track progress: Most critical aspect of learning is understand gaps, in order to understand gaps, self evaluation & tracking progress plays a major role. No digital products in the market is currently addressing this.
Community learning: Enable meaningful and frictionless interactions during potential moments learning collaboration between peers, experts & x aspirants.
These were some of the basis for building the information architecture.
Feature value adds

This activity was conducted to identify the unique and distinctive features which will best suit Manorama Yearbook online platform. This is an exhaustive list of features that can help users resonate with their needs & help stand out from any competition.
Information architecture
We focused on identifying distinctive ways of organising structuring, and labelling content in an effective and sustainable way. The goal is to help users find information and complete tasks.

Action driven IA: This Information Architecture is structured using bottom to top approach which involves grouping the information in desired buckets to bring out the need, aspirations and gap areas essential for the users. The objective was by identifying the opportunity areas structuring new ideas & features for the platform
Purpose driven IA: This Information Architecture is structured based on understanding users different needs and the purpose behind seeking information on various stages involved.
Purpose driven, Information architecture
Concepts
An ideal product experience is single stop shop for all its users needs. We visualised 5 navigation concepts that targeted pain points & added moments of delight within the ideal product experience.
Navigation concepts
Wireframes
We created a robust information architecture to help the users find the information they seek while ensuring a way to provide new content that may be relevant contextually.

Moving away from the conventional news browsing where the breaking news disrupts the reading flow, we sought to give users a new editorial experience by letting them seamlessly see the current affairs along with curated topics.
The unique content layout provides a distinct product identity for the brand, making it stand out amongst other news media platforms.
Final outcome
Responsive web, Native IOS & Android apps
Impact

The layout and architecture of the platform witnessed a drastic rise in the level of engagement in terms of the browsing and reading experience. Moreover, the effects of digitalization also boosted the sales of the physical copy books.
The numbers of subscribers increased to over 30,000 aspirants who use the platform not only as a source for knowledge but a learning tool.

caseStudies.title: Deccan Herald
caseStudies.subtitle: Helping a legacy a media brand get on the digital bandwagon.

blocks.text: Background

Deccan Herald (DH) is an English daily newspaper published from the Indian state of Karnataka by The Printers (Mysore) Private Limited, with a daily readership of 5.6 m readers nationally. The paradigm shift of readers to digital news media consumption urged the brand to get on the bandwagon to keep their loyal users happy. The objective is also to expand their reach to younger demography, while satisfying their existing loyal users. Our job was to create a product that not only resonate the brand legacy but also to maintain comfortable unique experience.
My Team & Role

I am the design strategist in the project, My responsibilities were: to be in touch with the board of directors & other key stakeholders of the company & define a vision to achieve the objectives. Set direction for the team, monitor the progress time to time, set research frame work, set guidelines for the team, involve hands on & help team in design detailing, mentor team for successful execution. My team involved 2 design researchers, 3 designers & 1 design lead:
Challenges

The marketplace of mobile news application is already saturated with lot of aggregators as well as publishing houses. Numerous formats of news are already available to the users. This narrows the window of opportunity to a new entrant.

Another major challenge is of introducing new concepts. Since the brand is quite late in this space, so it finds it difficult to try unique new feature so as not be disregarded as a stranger but at the same time comfortably maintains its uniqueness.
Approach: Research driven approach, followed with intensive collaboration with key client stakeholders.
Research & synthesis
Research process
Research intent

The research was conducted in order to understand the current mental model in news consumption given the landscape, to find out any unaddressed issues in the personal news consumption, to gather insights that can help design break the saturated market,

Areas of inquiry

In the overall digital news consumption, I identified three areas of inquiry: each areas is further broken down to multiple other areas. This helped us gather insights in a structured manner without any distractions. Also helps in prioritising research areas.

Research was conducted 3 locations in India: the research is done in tier 1 & 2 cities in India. We shortlisted users based on demographics & reading habits, in total total number of participants for the research were 36.

Shaping experience
Information architecture
Current IA is not role based, hence there is data clutter. Role based IA enabled clarity of information for end users.
Design directions

Region centric: Providing the higher level information that user needs pivoting to regions, this concept is minimal and task based. It gives a quick update and doesn’t overwhelm the user with all information at once
Data list: This concepts gives a list of data points that the user will want to monitor and in case it is required, user can drill down to a detailed view.
Tiled: Everything stacked together, still giving a hierarchy of information through fonts and UI, TILE is the simplest way to monitor every detail of your business.

Conventional: A familiar but effective approach using familiar design patterns, where user can see all data in a single page without any navigation with overlay drill downs so that user doesn’t loose the context.
Mapping general trends
Digital design trends are observed that are accepted widely and these trends makes platform a mark higher and hence make you stand out in the competition.
